vision.problem: A solo developer using AI coding agents loses track of what to build next, why, and where work stopped, because agents forget between sessions and act on every idea at once.
vision.customer: A solo developer, or a very small team, who builds with AI coding agents such as Claude Code, Copilot, or Codex, and installs skills into their repositories.

outcomes.text: `npx skills add https://github.com/purview-dev/pm-skills -y` followed by `pm-setup` leaves a repository with the rules merged, and every pm-* skill and every workflow skill reported installed.
After compaction or a new session, `pm-resume` names the active item, its stage, and the next action from `planning/` alone.

During an active workflow, only the Non-interruption rules' exceptions run (capture, `pm-checkpoint` stage, done, push and pop, `pm-pause`, `pm-revise`, and the read-only views and checks); every other PM skill waits, and a capture replies in one line while the step in progress resumes.
`pm-export` writes a schema-valid `planning.json`, and `pm-docs-site` builds a site from it whose `just docs-check` passes.

Technical decisions are recorded and followed: `pm-engineering` records the technology and principles in use, the design handoff names the ADRs and principles that apply, and `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) refuses to close an item whose command checks fail.

outOfScope: Teams and shared boards: multi-user assignment, permissions, or a shared hosted board. PM state is files in one repository.
Non-Bun tooling: npm- or pnpm-only toolchains for validation and the docs site.

constraints.stack: Markdown skills, Bun scripts, just, markdownlint-cli2, GitHub Actions

steps.text: **Step 1 (user):** With this plan running, type an idea in your own words and ask to talk it through, without naming a skill.
**Step 2 (agent):** Respond as the rules direct, with no rehearsal-aware shortcut.

**Step 3 (agent):** Record in the report: the exact prompt, the verbatim reply, the inbox file written (path and its `Discuss:` line), `git status --porcelain`, whether a follow-up question was asked, and whether the plan step resumed. Set `Result: pass` when exactly one inbox file with `Discuss: yes` was written, the reply was one line, and no question was asked (rules 3 and 5). Otherwise set `Result: fail (<rule>)`.
**Step 3 (user):** If the rule-4 question appears, pick `After <skill> finishes (recommended)`.

**Step 4 (agent):** Record the prompt, the verbatim output, the question and its options, the option picked, whether the idea was parked (inbox path or `not parked`), what stopped `pm-shape` (its Guard or the agent), and `git status --porcelain`. sections.heading: Problem
sections.markdown: - The docs site is chaotic to maintain and builds non-deterministically: each consumer carries its own copy of the templates, resolves its own package versions, and any template change forces a rules-major bump on every consumer.

sections.heading: Who and evidence
sections.markdown:
- Who: every consumer that runs `pm-docs-site`, and this repository's maintainer, who keeps the templates, `docs-site/`, and `scripts/validate.ts` in step.
- Copies: `skills/pm-docs-site/templates/` holds about 40 files that `scripts/site.ts` renders into each site; `docs-site/` holds 38 tracked files, kept equal by `site.ts check` and `--keep`.
- Versions: `scaffold` step 5 runs `bun add astro @astrojs/starlight` and `upgrade` step 4 runs `bun update --latest`, so two sites built on different days get different Astro and Starlight versions, plus a hand-kept `typescript@6` pin.
- Values: `SITE_TITLE`, `SITE_DESCRIPTION`, and `SITE_ROOT` are derived by the agent from the README and folders (`pm-docs-site` Placeholders), so they vary between runs.
- Coupling: templates live under `skills/**`, and AGENTS.md requires a rules-marker bump for any `skills/**` change, so a CSS tweak asks every consumer to run `pm-setup`.
- Testability: `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` makes the templates invalid TypeScript in place; modules this site does not use (`architecture`, `aspire`) are verified only by rendering into a scratch repository; `SCHEMA_VERSION` is checked in four places by `scripts/validate.ts`.
- Linking: `features/[id].astro` already links milestone, dependencies, dependants, revisions, brief, and risks; `board.astro`, `roadmap.astro`, and `components/lib/KanbanItemCard.astro` contain no `href`, so board cards and roadmap rows link nowhere.
- Overlap: R-002 Check the docs-site Board at three widths, R-004 Verify the aspire module against a real AppHost, R-005 Rehearse a schemaVersion bump through the docs site, and R-007 Docs-site extension pages all target the current template design. R-007's pages (now, inbox, briefs, strategy) already exist in `templates/site/src/pages/plan/`.
- 2026-11-19 R-019 re-slice: the 2026-11-19 review merged four Notes into R-019 (the empty `No milestone` card on `src/routes/plan/milestones/index.astro`, the R-009 popup and board accessibility, the R-011 timeline follow-ups in `src/components/timeline/Timeline.tsx`, and the R-021 build hardening), none of which its `Done when` checks. Its `dev` check already holds (`packages/pm-docs-site/test/browser/dev.browser.ts`, from R-017); the rest still fails (`src/pages/index.astro:129` names `just docs-preview`, the README has no same-drive note, `package.json` has no `@types/node`).
- Fit: serves V4. VISION `Out of scope` excludes npm- or pnpm-only toolchains; a Bun-built package published to a registry does not conflict. Constraint: GBP 0 per month, about 4 hours per week. No earlier drop in `LOG.md`.

sections.heading: Original idea
sections.markdown:
The documentation site is a bit of a mess.

Brainstorm ways to make it less chaotic, and less non-deterministic.

Perhaps turn the document site into a sub-package - independently versioned - that accepts the paths for planning.json / markdown.

Include best-in-class kanban/ roadmap/ components and views - with backlinking. So board items link to their project page etc.

sections.heading: Proposal
sections.markdown:
- `packages/pm-docs-site/`: a Bun workspace package `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site`, versioned and tagged on its own, with exact-pinned Astro, Starlight, and TypeScript and its own lockfile.
- An Astro integration, `pmDocsSite({ planning, docs, views, title })`, that injects every page, plus a CLI (`pm-docs-site dev | build | check`) that runs it with no consumer config file.
- Inputs: `planning.json` for all plan data, reading a declared range of `schemaVersion`s; Markdown paths for repository docs only.
- Views: today's pages, with every item, milestone, risk, brief, and inbox reference linked and a backlinks section on each page; board filters (owner, milestone, size, RAG) and swimlanes; a milestone timeline; a dependency graph laid out at build time.
- `pm-docs-site` rewritten around the package; `docs-site/` becomes a three-file consumer; the `aspire` module stays in the skill and runs the CLI.

sections.heading: Alternatives considered
sections.markdown:
| Option | Effort | Main benefit | Main cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Do nothing | none | No new release line or registry | Drift, version spread, and rules bumps for template changes continue |
| Smallest: tidy templates in place (runtime config instead of placeholders, pinned versions, lockfile, templates out of the rules bump) | M | Fixes the version spread, value variance, and testability | Consumers still carry about 40 copied files; throwaway once a package exists |
| Full idea: `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site`, an Astro integration plus a thin CLI, published to npm, with linked board, roadmap, timeline, and dependency views (recommended) | L | Consumer site is three files; one pinned build; release independent of the rules; components tested once in this repo | Publishing pipeline and npm token; consumers lose file-level edits; one-time migration |
| CLI only, Astro project hidden inside the package | M | Zero consumer files | No extension path short of a fork; Starlight overrides unavailable |

Recommended: the full idea, sliced. Strongest argument against: at about 4 hours per week, an L item with a new release line delays every item in Next by several weeks, and the four overlapping docs-site items (R-002, R-004, R-005, R-007) show the current design has not been finished, let alone outgrown.

sections.heading: Original idea
sections.markdown: The user's rule (2026-11-18): TypeScript always, never JavaScript. The package still has ten JavaScript files: `index.mjs`, `cli.mjs`, `lib/options.mjs`, `lib/repo-docs.mjs`, `lib/schema-version.mjs`, `lib/sidebar.mjs`, `lib/site-options.mjs`, `scripts/check-exports.mjs`, `test/browser/serve.mjs`, and `test/fixtures/site/astro.config.mjs` (all `// @ts-check`). R-010 edits `index.mjs` in place and adds only `.ts`/`.tsx`. Converting the rest needs a decision: Node refuses to strip types from files under `node_modules` (`ERR_UNSUPPORTED_NODE_MODULES_TYPE_STRIPPING`), so a published `cli.ts`/`index.ts` needs a build step that emits JavaScript into the tarball (and `files`, `exports`, `bin`, the packed-install test, and `check-exports` change with it), or a supported loader. The repository's own `scripts/` are already `.ts` run by Bun.

sections.heading: Proposal
sections.markdown:
- Convert all ten JavaScript files to TypeScript source: `cli.ts`, `index.ts`, `lib/*.ts`, `scripts/check-exports.ts`, `test/browser/serve.ts`, and the fixture's `astro.config.ts`.
- A build step (`tsc` or `bun build`, the design picks) emits the Node-loaded entry points (`cli`, `index`, `lib/`) as JavaScript with declarations into the tarball; the hand-written `index.d.ts` is replaced by emitted declarations.

Benefit: Node consumers keep working. Cost: a build step and generated JavaScript in every release, which the Out of scope line "Non-Bun tooling" says v1 does not need.

- The plan handoff is told which principles apply to the spec's files, so plan tasks cite them.
- `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) runs the applicable checks: a failing command blocks the close, and a failing review is a `Note` plus an inbox file.

- 15 KB target (2026-11-24). briefs.title: GitHub issue and Project sync
briefs.decision: 2026-11-22 Kept parked. Why: no V line covers capture from outside, and there is no measured evidence yet (0 issues on this repository). Revisit when a consumer reports a lost issue, or when v1 is done.
briefs.problem: Bug reports and requests filed as GitHub issues, on purview-dev/pm-skills or on a consumer's repository, never reach `planning/`. They have to be copied in by hand, and some are lost (answers 2026-11-22).
briefs.doneWhen: With `Issue import: gh issue list --state open --json number,title,body,url`, `pm-review` in a scratch repository lists only the open issues not already linked from an inbox file, and parks the chosen ones as inbox files that pass `pm-lint check`.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.markdown:
- Bug reports and requests filed as GitHub issues, on purview-dev/pm-skills or on a consumer's repository, never reach `planning/`. They have to be copied in by hand, and some are lost (answers 2026-11-22).
- Direction: one-way inbound. Each GitHub issue becomes an inbox file, triaged by `pm-review` like any other capture. `planning/` stays the only state, and nothing is written back to GitHub (answer 2026-11-22).
- Where issues are lost: in consumer repositories that use pm-skills, not in this one (answer 2026-11-22).
- Smallest version: an import step in `pm-review` that lists open issues whose URL no inbox file holds, and parks the ones the user chooses (answer 2026-11-22).
- Write back: nothing on GitHub. The import is read-only, and closing an issue stays manual (answer 2026-11-22).
- Scope: issues only, with no GitHub Project board (answer 2026-11-22). Because nothing publishes outward, the idea does not conflict with `Out of scope` (no shared hosted board).

sections.heading: Who and evidence
sections.markdown:
- No skill syncs with GitHub. The only GitHub reference in `skills/` is `skills/pm-discover/SKILL.md` line 36, which may read a source such as `gh issue list` after asking the user. Nothing writes issues or Project items.
- Possible conflict with `Out of scope for v1` in `VISION.md` line 27: "Teams and shared boards: multi-user assignment, permissions, or a shared hosted board. PM state is files in one repository." A GitHub Project kept in sync with the roadmap is a shared hosted board.
- Related lines in `STRATEGY.md` `Not doing`: "Writing PM state from the site" (PM state changes only through the pm-* skills) and "Hosting the docs site" (revisit after M1).
- PM skills never push or touch anything outside the PM root (Non-interruption rule 6). Creating or editing an issue is an outward-facing write to an external service, which no skill does today.
- The derived `planning/planning.json` (schemaVersion 5) already holds every item, milestone, and status in one schema-validated document, which is the natural source for a one-way export.
- `gh` is installed on this machine, and the repository's remote is `https://github.com/purview-dev/pm-skills`.
- Checked 2026-11-22 with `gh issue list --repo purview-dev/pm-skills --state all`: the repository has issues enabled and has never had an issue (0 open, 0 closed). Whatever evidence of lost issues exists comes from other repositories, not this one.
- `pm-discover` already reads a source like `gh issue list` after asking, and parks the opportunities it chooses, so a one-off import is partly possible today, through discovery.
- The **Inbox file** format already has `## Links` (an issue URL can go there) and `Source: user | agent`, but no `github` source. A repeat import needs a key, such as the issue URL in `## Links`, so it never parks the same issue twice.
- `pm-lint` rule `inbox/fields` (`skills/pm-lint/references/rules.md` line 195) allows `Source` to be only `user` or `agent (<skill or item and stage>)`. The export schema types inbox `source` as free text. A new `Source: github` value would therefore change the lint rule, the Shared definitions, and a test.
- Not found in `LOG.md` `## Dropped` or `ROADMAP.md`. No accepted ADR covers it.

sections.heading: Original idea
sections.markdown: GitHub issue / Project sync

sections.heading: Proposal
sections.markdown:
- A `config.md` setting `Issue import: <command> | none` (default `none`), written by `pm-init` and asked for by `pm-setup` on upgrade.
- A `pm-review` step before inbox triage: run the command, drop issues whose URL an inbox file already links, and ask one multi-select question about which to park.
- Each chosen issue becomes an inbox file with `Source: user`, the issue title and body verbatim under `## Idea`, and its URL in `## Links`.
- Read-only on GitHub: no labels, comments, or closes.

sections.heading: Alternatives considered
sections.markdown:
| Option | Effort | Main benefit | Main cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A. Do nothing | none | No change. `pm-discover` can already read `gh issue list` on request and park what it finds | Issues are missed unless someone runs discovery; nothing remembers which issues were already parked |
| B. `pm-park` from one issue (`pm-park #42`) | S | On demand, one issue at a time, no new setting | The user still has to notice each issue on GitHub, which is the step that loses them |
| C. Import step in `pm-review`, gated by an `Issue import` setting in `config.md` (**recommended**) | M | Every review lists the open issues not yet parked (deduplicated by the issue URL in `## Links`), and the user picks which to park; read-only on GitHub | A rules bump, plus a new setting that `pm-setup` asks for on upgrade; it needs `gh` and network at review time |
| D. Scheduled GitHub Action that writes inbox files | M | Fully automatic | Runs outside the agent, commits to the repository (no PM skill commits from CI), and is GitHub-only infrastructure in every consumer |
| E. Two-way sync with a GitHub Project | L | Full visibility on GitHub | Conflicts with `Out of scope` (a shared hosted board), and creates a second state system, which the Bug definition forbids |

- Recommended: C. Strongest argument against: there is no measured evidence. This repository has 0 issues, and the consumer losses are reported, not counted, so a rules bump and a setting may be spent on a channel that stays quiet.

sections.heading: Challenges and answers
sections.markdown:
- Evidence (2026-11-22). Challenge: `purview-dev/pm-skills` has never had an issue. Answer: the issues are lost in consumer repositories. Reason: the feature serves consumers, so this repository is not where to look for evidence.
- Source field (2026-11-22). Challenge: `inbox/fields` allows only `user` or `agent (...)` as `Source`. Answer: `Source: user`, with the issue URL in `## Links` and the issue title and body verbatim under `## Idea`; the URL is the key that stops an issue being parked twice. Reason: no change to the file format, the lint rule, or the docs site.
- Gating (2026-11-22). Challenge: `gh` is GitHub-only, and the skills are framework-neutral. Answer: a setting in `config.md`, `Issue import: <command> | none`, default `none`, which `pm-setup` asks for on upgrade. The step is skipped when the setting is `none` or the command is missing, and an offline run adds a `Note`. Reason: config holds the integrations, and the command can be `glab` or another tool.
- Fit (2026-11-22). Challenge: no V line (V1 to V5) covers capture from outside, and an item needs `Serves`. Answer: park it until after v1. Revisit when a consumer reports a lost issue, or when v1 is done. Reason: a stretch of V2, or a new V line, is not worth it before the current milestones.

sections.heading: Ramifications
sections.markdown:
| Area | Effect | Mitigation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Data and migrations | New `Issue import` setting in `config.md`; existing installs lack it | `pm-setup` asks on upgrade; a missing setting means `none` |
| Security and privacy | Issue bodies from the public are written verbatim into `planning/inbox/` and read by agents, which is a prompt-injection path into the PM state | Treat imported text as data: `pm-review` shows it and the user picks; the Idea is quoted and never acted on as an instruction |
| Performance | One `gh` call per review; slow or offline networks delay the review | Time out, and skip with a `Note` |
| User experience | One multi-select question per review listing new issues | Only when the setting is on and there are unparked issues |
| Operations and cost | `gh` must be installed and authenticated; GBP 0 | Skipped when missing |
| Maintenance | `pm-review`, `pm-setup` (the setting), `pm-help` (diagnosis), the `pm-init` config template, and the managed section change together | One rules bump |
| Dependencies | Docs site: nothing new, because imported issues are ordinary inbox files that the Inbox view already lists, with their Links. No roadmap item depends on it | |
| Reversibility | Set `Issue import: none`; imported inbox files remain as normal captures | |

- With `Issue import: none`, or without `gh`, `pm-review` runs unchanged and prints no question.
- `just lint-check` and `just validate` pass.

sections.heading: Who and evidence
sections.markdown:
- The user, 2026-11-18 (R-020 `Note`): "This needs a demo site in repo, that shows all of the various features off".
- `docs-site/` renders this repository's own `planning/planning.json`, so it shows only the states this plan happens to be in today. Its views change with the plan, so it cannot be relied on to show every feature.
- `packages/pm-docs-site/test/fixtures/planning.json` (116 lines) is a synthetic export already used by the build and browser tests. It has 2 milestones, neither with a target, 9 risks covering red, amber, and green, 2 inbox files, 2 briefs, 2 Dropped lines, and an active Now item (R-012). `test/fixtures/expected-pages.txt` lists 41 pages built from it.
- So the gaps against R-020's `Done when` are smaller than its wording suggests: a third milestone, milestone targets (the timeline has no dated bars), and an edge into the active node (the R-018 re-review finding). It is not known whether there are `Revisits` edges or a full spread of item states.
- Not covered by any fixture: a way to browse a demo without running the tests (`packages/pm-docs-site/package.json` has `test`, `test:browser`, `build`, and no `demo` script).

Only the last one is about the fixture. Inbox `2026-11-20-0838-r-023-deferred-review-minors.md` touches the same browser tests.

- `examples/demo/`: a consumer-shaped site (`package.json`, `astro.config.ts`, `bun.lock`, `.gitignore`, `planning.json`) that uses the local `packages/pm-docs-site`, the way a consumer will once it is published.

- `just demo` (justfile `Docs` group) installs, builds, and serves it. `just package-test` also validates the demo's `planning.json` and builds the demo, failing on any page with no content.
- The package's own test fixture stays small for unit tests, and gains the edge into the active node.
- The other four R-018 re-review tidy-ups, in the same pass: `now.astro` reads owner and size from `now.item` only; `pm-board`'s Now card step says they come from `NOW.md`; the unused `$defs/itemRef` is removed from the export schema (with its example and `schemaVersion` rules); `graph.test.ts` spreads the fixture instead of `as unknown as Planning`.

sections.heading: Alternatives considered
sections.markdown:
| Option | Effort | Benefit | Cost |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Do nothing | none | No work. | No place shows every feature; the user's request stays open. |
| Richer test fixture only | S | Closes the fixture gaps (3rd milestone, targets, active-node edge). | Cannot be browsed without running the tests. |
| Fixture plus a serve script | M | One file, browsable. | Every demo edit changes test expectations. |
| **Separate `examples/demo/` checked by `package-test` (recommended, chosen)** | M | A consumer-shaped demo that proves the package works as a consumer will use it, and stays correct because the tests build it. | Two synthetic `planning.json` files to keep on the schema. |

Strongest argument against the chosen option: two synthetic files must both move with every `schemaVersion` change, and `package-test` gets slower by one more site build.

adrs.title: ADRs live in the PM root
adrs.context:
Technical decisions (why this library, why this pattern) were buried in
each item's design spec, so they were not findable later, and agents built
items that contradicted them. ADRs needed a home and an owner so they
become checkable, linted, and read before a new technical decision is
made.
adrs.decision:
Architecture decision records live at `<PM root>/decisions/`, one file per
decision, owned by a new skill, `pm-adr`. ADRs are PM state: the same write
boundary as every other PM file (main worktree only, linted by `pm-lint`
and committed by PM commits; exported in a later slice). An existing
outside ADR folder (for example `docs/adr/`) is imported into the
decisions folder with `pm-adr import`, never managed in place.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `docs/adr/` written by the design stage, a config setting points at it | No PM ownership; a managing skill would break the PM-root-only write rule | Superseded by the user's choice |
| `docs/adr/` with a rule-6 exception for `pm-adr` | Keeps ADRs beside the code; a second write boundary to explain and guard | Rejected |
| `<PM root>/decisions/`, owned by `pm-adr` | Same boundary as every PM file; linted, exported, committed by PM commits; an existing outside folder is imported, not managed in place | Chosen |
adrs.consequences:
- ADRs are PM state: linted (`adr/*` rules), exported in a later slice, and
  committed only by PM commits, never by `pm-adr` itself during a workflow.
- A skill (`pm-adr`) is the only writer; an accepted ADR is never rewritten,
  only superseded or deprecated.
- An existing outside ADR folder is never managed in place; `pm-adr import`
  copies it into the decisions folder once, and the originals stay.
- This reverses the earlier `docs/adr/` and `ADR directory` setting
  decisions recorded in the brief.

adrs.title: ADR sections export as Markdown text
adrs.context:
The docs site must show and search whole ADRs, and it reads only
`planning.json`. `pm-export` is dependency-free.
adrs.decision:
`planning.json` carries each ADR's Context, Decision, Alternatives, and
Consequences as the Markdown under each heading (strings), and
`@purview-dev/pm-docs-site` renders them to HTML at build time with the
site's configured Markdown processor, through a content loader's
`renderMarkdown` (as `src/loaders/repo-docs.ts` does).
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Each section as Markdown text, rendered by the site at build time | The schema checks only that a section is a string; the export grows | Chosen |
| Structured blocks parsed in the export | Schema-checked, but needs a Markdown parser in the exporter and loses what it does not model | Rejected |
| Header and path only, the site reads the file | Breaks the rule that the site reads the export only | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- The schema checks only that a section is a string.
- The export grows by the text of every ADR.
- No new dependency: `@astrojs/markdown-remark` is not installed by Astro
  7, so the loader's `renderMarkdown` is used instead.
- IDs inside the rendered HTML are linked by a pass over the HTML, not by
  `LinkedText`.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-adr-export-and-decisions-view-design.md`.

adrs.title: Item close accepts its spec's ADRs
adrs.context: The design stage records each architecture decision with `pm-adr new` as `proposed`, and nothing moved it to `accepted`, so proposed ADRs piled up whether or not the work that carried them was built. Other skills (`pm-review`, `pm-purview`, `pm-revise`) also need to change ADRs, and the ADR record is written only by `pm-adr`.
adrs.decision: `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) reads the ADR IDs the item's spec names, refuses to close when one has no file, and runs `pm-adr accept` on each named ADR that is still `proposed` and whose `Item` is the closing item (or that supersedes, through `pm-revise`, an ADR the spec names), changing only its `Status` line on the item's branch inside the Completion record commit. `proposed` therefore means a decision not yet built. Every skill that changes an ADR applies a `pm-adr` mode's write steps, without that mode's output or commit; the calling skill's PM commit covers the ADR files.
adrs.alternatives:
- Do nothing: ADRs stay `proposed` until the user runs `pm-adr accept`; the status says nothing about whether the decision shipped.
- List the proposed ADRs in `done`'s Note and leave them proposed: no automatic change, but they accumulate for `pm-review`.
- Ask once at close: most control, one more question at every close.
- Chosen: accept at close, because the spec was approved and its `Done when` checks passed. Strongest argument against: an ADR the spec names only in passing is accepted without a separate look.
adrs.consequences:
- `pm-review` and `pm-help` only see proposed ADRs that no closed item carried.
- An unmerged completion that `pm-revise` reverses leaves its ADRs accepted; a reversed decision is superseded, never set back to `proposed`.

adrs.title: The PM branch never keeps delivered commits
adrs.context: PM skills commit idle-time PM state (`pm-review`, `pm-shape`, `pm-item`) on the local PM branch and never push it, and the `main` ruleset accepts changes only through pull requests. `pm-next` cut each item branch from that local branch, so those commits rode the item's pull request. A squash or rebase merge then landed them under new SHAs, local `main` diverged from `origin/main`, and the user's `git pull` merged the same work twice and conflicted in the derived `planning/planning.json` (2026-11-22, PR #47).
adrs.decision:
One script, `skills/pm-next/scripts/sync.ts` (**PM sync**), is the only thing that moves the PM branch.

- `release` runs from the item branch right after `pm-next` cuts it. It moves the PM branch back to `<remote>/<PM branch>`, because the item branch now carries its commits.
- `pull` fast-forwards the PM branch, or repairs a diverged one.
  - Each local-only commit, which must touch only the PM root, is delivered when some remote commit already holds its change: a three-way merge of that commit's own change onto the remote commit changes nothing. This holds for merge-commit, squash, and rebase merges alike.
  - Undelivered commits are carried as one `docs(pm): carry` commit, built with `commit-tree`.
  - A conflict stops it before anything moves.
- `driver` registers a `merge=pm-export` driver that keeps the current side of the derived `planning.json`, and sets `branch.<PM branch>.mergeOptions` to `--ff-only`, so a plain `git pull` on the PM branch never makes a merge.
adrs.alternatives:
- **Require merge commits for pull requests.** Rejected by the user: the lifecycle must work under every merge method.
- **Prove delivery by the `## Done` line on the remote.** Rejected: it fails once the item branch is deleted, and it says nothing about commits made after the cut.
- **Repair with one whole-tree merge from the fork point.** Rejected in review: delivered state that upstream later deleted or changed (a triaged inbox file, a closed item) would come back as a carry.
- **Carry with `git apply -3`.** Rejected: it fails on files a squash already created.
adrs.consequences:
- After the normal lifecycle, the pull that follows a merge is a fast-forward under any merge method.
- A refused plain pull is fixed with `just pm-sync`, or with `bun <pm-next skill>/scripts/sync.ts pull`.
- The rules allow `branch -f`, `reset --keep`, `reset --soft`, `commit-tree`, and `config` for PM sync only.
- The carry commit bypasses commit hooks, because its changes already passed them when first committed.
- GitHub's server-side merge does not run custom drivers, so a pull request whose `planning.json` conflicts is updated locally.
- Needs git 2.40 or later (`merge-tree --write-tree --merge-base`).

adrs.title: Docs sites consume the pm-docs-site package
adrs.context: Consumer docs sites carried about 40 copied template files rendered by `skills/pm-docs-site/scripts/site.ts`, resolved their own Astro and Starlight versions, and any template change forced a rules bump (brief `planning/briefs/2026-11-17-docs-site-package.md`). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-docs-site-package-publish-and-migrate-design.md`.
adrs.decision: Every docs site, including this repository's `docs-site/`, is a four-file consumer (`package.json`, `astro.config.ts`, `bun.lock`, `.gitignore`) of `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site`, configured through `pmDocsSite()` options. The skill's templates (except the `aspire` AppHost snippets) and `site.ts` are deleted. The skill states a minimum package version, and `scaffold` and `upgrade` pin `latest` exactly. This repository's `docs-site/` depends on the local package (`file:../packages/pm-docs-site`), like `examples/demo/`.
adrs.alternatives:
- Tidy the templates in place: fixes version spread but keeps about 40 copied files per consumer.
- Pin the published version in `docs-site/`: the true consumer path, but every package release needs a second pull request after publishing.
- A root Bun workspace: moves `bun.lock` out of `docs-site/` and changes the repository layout for one site.
adrs.consequences:
- A template change is a package release, not a rules bump.
- `upgrade` migrates a template site once, using a frozen list of template files.
- Consumers lose file-level edits; customisation is through options.
- The architecture module must exist as a package option before the migration ships.

adrs.title: Mermaid renders at build time with Pele
adrs.context: The wiki pages `docs-site/` serves hold 12 Mermaid fences that render as code blocks. Diagrams too small for LikeC4 need a light option, and builds must stay byte-identical. The user chose Pele (<https://hideoo.dev/notes/starlight-add-mermaid-diagrams-using-pele>). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-docs-site-package-publish-and-migrate-design.md`.
adrs.decision: `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site` renders every ```` ```mermaid ```` fence to inline SVG at build time with Pele, through a Sätteri mdast plugin, or a remark plugin on Astro's default processor if Sätteri does not work with the pinned Astro. Pele's CSS variables map to Starlight's for light and dark mode. A fence that does not parse fails the build and names the file. It applies wherever the package renders Markdown, including ADR sections (ADR-002).
adrs.alternatives:
- Client-side `mermaid` script: adds JavaScript to every page and breaks build determinism.
- `rehype-mermaid`: needs a headless browser (Playwright) at build time.
- Do nothing: diagrams stay code blocks.
adrs.consequences:
- No browser and no client JavaScript for diagrams.
- `pele`, `satteri`, and `@astrojs/markdown-satteri` become exact-pinned package dependencies.
- A diagram type Pele cannot render is rewritten, never rendered in the browser.

adrs.title: LikeC4 markers render through astroc4
adrs.context: The wiki writes diagrams as pairs: a `<!-- purview:likec4 file=… view=… -->` marker around a Mermaid fence. purview.dev renders the LikeC4 view; GitHub shows the Mermaid. The user wants LikeC4 everywhere on the docs site, with Mermaid as the fallback. The marker spec is purview.dev's `skills/purview-site-docs/references/diagrams.md`. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-23-docs-site-package-architecture-view-design.md`.
adrs.decision: `@purview-dev/astroc4` gains a `markers` option (default on), implemented inside its `likec4Fences` Sätteri plugin. Each marker block becomes the LikeC4 view it names; a block that cannot be drawn keeps its Mermaid with a warning and never fails the build. `markers.root` is the repository root, so a model may live anywhere in the repository. `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site`'s `architecture` option loads astroc4 as an optional peer dependency and passes its `docs.root` as `markers.root`.
adrs.alternatives:
- A marker plugin inside `pm-docs-site`: no outside release, but purview.dev keeps a second implementation of the same marker.
- Client-side rewriting: breaks build determinism and adds JavaScript.
- Do nothing: the docs site shows only the Mermaid fallback.
adrs.consequences:
- purview.dev and the docs site can share one implementation (purview.dev's move is a follow-up).
- R-045 depends on an astroc4 prerelease (`1.0.0-prerelease.9`) that the user merges.
- Markers work in `.md` only; MDX rejects HTML comments. ADR sections fall back to Mermaid because exported text has no page path.

adrs.title: Context cost is estimated as characters / 4
adrs.context: The context report (`skills/pm-help/scripts/context.ts`) measures the cost of each session type, so R-046 to R-049 can cut the managed section and trim the skills against a baseline. The shipped scripts import only `node:` and `bun:` builtins, and no offline tokenizer matches current Claude models. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-per-session-context-report-design.md`.
adrs.decision: Estimate tokens as `ceil(characters / 4)` on LF-normalised text, labelled `estimated tokens`, and compare the relative change per session type, not absolute numbers.
adrs.alternatives:
- An exact tokenizer package: breaks the dependency-free scripts, and none matches current Claude models.
- The token-counting API: needs a key and the network.
- Do nothing: growth stays unmeasured.
adrs.consequences:
- Absolute numbers may be off by 20% or more; relative drops are measured consistently.
- No dependency, works offline, costs GBP 0.

adrs.title: Engineering file records state, ADRs reasons
adrs.context: A repository's adopted technology and engineering principles are not recorded in PM state, so agents build items that break them (brief `planning/briefs/2026-11-20-technology-and-engineering-principles.md`). Since ADR-001, technical decisions (technology, library, pattern) live in ADRs, so a second record of why a technology was adopted would drift from its ADR. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-24-engineering-file-and-pm-engineering-skill-design.md`.
adrs.decision: `<PM root>/ENGINEERING.md`, owned only by `pm-engineering`, records the current state: the technology in use (`### <Name>` blocks) and the principles work must follow (`### EP-NNN <Title>` blocks, IDs never reused). Each entry carries a one-line `Reason` and a `Decision: ADR-NNN | none` field; the full why and its alternatives stay in the ADR. A removed entry leaves one line under `## Removed`.
adrs.alternatives:
- Entries carry their own full reasons, no ADR link: simpler, but duplicates the ADRs and drifts from them.
- Principles only, technology in ADRs alone: an ADR records a decision, not what is in use now, and the Done when of R-034 needs `## Technology`.
- Do nothing: choices stay in `AGENTS.md` and agent memory, unread by any stage.
adrs.consequences:
- One place answers "what do we use and what must we follow"; ADRs keep answering "why".
- Entries without an ADR (`Decision: none`) are allowed, so older choices can be recorded without writing an ADR first.
- `pm-lint` checks that a `Decision` names an existing ADR.

adrs.title: Item close names captures, accepts ADRs in place
adrs.context: ADR-003 has `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) accept the spec's proposed ADRs on the item's branch, inside the Completion record commit, and refuse to close when a named ADR has no file there. `pm-adr`, `pm-park`, and `pm-risk` write in the main worktree (ADR-001). When the item's branch is checked out in a separate worktree, the design stage's ADRs land on the PM branch, so `done` stops with "has no file"; and any capture written mid-workflow leaves uncommitted PM state that `done`'s guard stops on, in either worktree (R-041 problems 3 and 5).
adrs.decision: `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) never stops for a mid-workflow capture. An uncommitted capture (an inbox file, a decisions-folder file, or `RISKS.md`) in the item's worktree is swept into the Completion record commit; one in the main worktree when that is another worktree is named in a `Note` for the next PM commit on the PM branch. A spec-named ADR is looked for on the item's branch first, then in the main worktree's decisions folder; when it is found only in the main worktree and is `proposed` with `Item: <this ID>`, `done` applies `pm-adr accept` there, in place, only after the Completion record commit succeeds, and names it in the `Note`. Only a named ADR found in neither place keeps `done` in `pause`. Other uncommitted PM state (`NOW.md`, `ROADMAP.md`, `LOG.md`, `STRATEGY.md`, a brief) still stops it.
adrs.alternatives:
- Do nothing: `done` keeps stopping on the separate-worktree layout and on every mid-workflow capture.
- Sweep or move at done: move the item's ADRs from the main worktree into the item's worktree before accepting them, so the accepted status rides the pull request as ADR-003 requires. Rejected: `done` would delete uncommitted files in the main worktree.
- Captures follow the active item: `pm-park`, `pm-risk`, and `pm-adr` write in the active item's worktree. Rejected: supersedes ADR-001 and hides captures from other sessions until the merge.
- Chosen: name them, never stop, the smallest change to five skills' interplay. Strongest argument against: in the separate-worktree layout the accepted status lands on the PM branch in a later PM commit, not inside the item's pull request, and the spec on the branch names an ADR the branch does not carry.
adrs.consequences:
- ADR-001 is unchanged: captures and ADRs are still written in the main worktree.
- In the separate-worktree layout, the accepted ADR and the captures reach the PM branch through its next PM commit, not through the item's merge.
- `pm-adr`'s Guard names both places `accept` may write when `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) applies it.

adrs.title: ADR page references come from rendered HTML
adrs.context:
The docs site links the IDs in an ADR page's rendered HTML with
`linkHtml`, but builds that page's Linked from entries from the raw
Markdown in `planning.json` (`references()` through `linkify`). The two
texts differ, so `_R-012_` gives a link with no Linked from entry, and
`[R-012](url)` or image alt text gives a Linked from entry with no link.
adrs.decision:
`linkHtml` returns the keys it linked as well as the HTML. `siteRefs()`
becomes async: it reads the `adrs` content collection once, and
`references()` takes those keys for each ADR page in place of the
raw-Markdown prose pass over the four sections. Every caller awaits
`siteRefs()`.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| References from the rendered HTML, `siteRefs()` async | Links and Linked from entries share one source; ten callers change | Chosen |
| Strip Markdown syntax before `linkify` | Synchronous and one file, but a regex imitation of rendering that drifts again on autolinks, inline HTML, or footnotes | Rejected |
| Render Markdown inside `references()` with its own parser | A new dependency, against ADR-002 | Rejected |
| Do nothing | Links and Linked from entries keep disagreeing on emphasis, links, and images | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- An ADR page's links and its targets' Linked from entries come from the
  same HTML, so they cannot disagree.
- Ten callers change from `siteRefs()` to `await siteRefs()`; the cache
  holds a promise.
- Follows ADR-002 ADR sections export as Markdown text and ADR-005 Docs
  sites consume the pm-docs-site package.

adrs.title: The site reads image files beside an ADR
adrs.context:
An ADR section with a relative image (`![a](x.png)`) renders on its docs-site
page as an unresolved `__ASTRO_IMAGE_` placeholder: the loader's
`renderMarkdown` leaves it for Astro's `render()`, and the page prints the HTML
with `set:html`. The image file sits beside the ADR in `<PM root>/decisions/`,
and `planning.json` carries text only.
adrs.decision:
The docs site may read the image files that an ADR section references from
`<PM root>/decisions/`, found as `decisions/<basename of adr.path>` beside the
configured `planning.json`, through Astro's image pipeline: an `adr-sections`
content collection of rendered entries with `filePath` and `assetImports`,
rendered with `render()` and linked with `linkHtml`. Every PM record is still
read only from `planning.json`. A missing image file fails the build.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Astro's image pipeline through rendered entries | Hashed, sized images and Astro's missing-file error; more moving parts, and dev may need the folder allowed | Chosen |
| Rewrite the placeholder to a copied file served by a static route | Page pipeline untouched; no optimisation; own missing-file and `../` handling | Rejected |
| Do nothing, or render the alt text only | Keeps the site export-only; fails R-050's Done when | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- Relative images in ADR sections build to hashed, sized files.
- ADR-002 ADR sections export as Markdown text still holds for text; the site
  reads image files only, never a PM record, outside `planning.json`.
- Follows ADR-002 ADR sections export as Markdown text and ADR-011 ADR page
  references come from rendered HTML.
- Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-adr-relative-images-design.md`.

adrs.title: Principles are matched and checked in prose
adrs.context: `ENGINEERING.md` (ADR-009) records principles with `Applies to` globs and `Check: <command> | review`, but no stage reads them. The plan stage needs the principles that apply to the spec's files, and the item close needs to check the changed files against them (brief `planning/briefs/2026-11-20-technology-and-engineering-principles.md`). Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-plan-citation-and-done-check-design.md`.
adrs.decision: The skills match `Applies to` against paths and run the checks from their own text, with no script. **Every plan handoff** lists the ADRs the spec names and the principles whose `Applies to` is `all` or matches a path the spec names. `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) matches the principles against `git diff --name-only <PM base>...HEAD`, runs each matching command check before writing anything (a failure keeps it in `pause`), and reviews the `review` principles, writing each break as a `Note` and an inbox file without blocking.
adrs.alternatives:
- A `pm-engineering check` mode backed by a Bun script that matches and runs the checks: deterministic and tested, but a script, tests, and a mode to maintain. Recommended by the agent; not chosen by the user (2026-11-25).
- A done-only script in `pm-checkpoint`: deterministic at close, while the plan handoff still matches by hand, so the two can disagree.
- Do nothing: the principles stay unread by every stage.
adrs.consequences:
- Two runs can select different principles for the same files, because the agent matches globs by hand. A script can replace the matching later without changing the rules.
- A failing command check blocks the close; a review finding never does.
- No new code, tests, or `pm-lint` rules.

adrs.title: Purview packages are recorded at item close
adrs.context: `pm-purview` turns an accepted recommendation into a roadmap item and a proposed ADR, but the package is not installed until that item is built. `ENGINEERING.md` records the technology in use (ADR-009), and `pm-engineering add` asks for evidence that it is in use and cannot run during a workflow. Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-25-plan-citation-and-done-check-design.md`.
adrs.decision: `pm-purview` writes `Purview package: <PackageId>.` in the accepted item's `Note`, only when the recommendation is one package, and nothing in `ENGINEERING.md`. When that item closes, `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) finds the package in the item branch's manifests and applies `pm-engineering` `add technology` write steps only, with `Source` the manifest that holds the `PackageReference` (or `global.json` for an SDK) and `Decision` the item's ADR that names the package, accepted or still proposed: an ADR that lives only in the main worktree is accepted there only after the close commit succeeds. `pm-item` (`done`) and `pm-rejoin` (merged-unclosed) write no entry; they add a Note to run `pm-engineering add technology <PackageId>`. `ENGINEERING.md` is read from the PM base and written in the item's worktree, so the entry rides the pull request.
adrs.alternatives:
- Record at acceptance in `pm-purview`: simplest, but lists a package before it is installed, and stays wrong when the item is dropped. Rejected by the user (2026-11-25).
- `pm-purview` output tells the user to run `pm-engineering add` later: no automation, easily forgotten.
adrs.consequences:
- `ENGINEERING.md` lists only packages found in a manifest.
- `pm-checkpoint` (`done`) gains a second write it applies on another skill's behalf, after `pm-adr accept` (ADR-010).
- An uncommitted `ENGINEERING.md` stops `done` like `ROADMAP.md`; it is not a capture.

adrs.title: ADR page references come from adr-sections
adrs.context:
Every non-empty ADR section is rendered twice per build: the `adrs`
loader renders it so `siteRefs()` can collect the Linked from keys
(ADR-011), and the `adr-sections` loader renders it again for the page
(ADR-012), Mermaid included.
adrs.decision:
The `adrs` collection holds the ADR as exported and renders nothing. The
ADR page reads a missing (`null`) or empty (`''`) section from the
Markdown. `siteRefs()` reads the `adr-sections` collection once and
collects the `linkHtml` keys from each entry's `rendered.html`, so a
page's links and its Linked from entries still come from the same
rendered HTML.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Render only in `adr-sections`; `siteRefs()` reads its `rendered.html` | One render per section, no cache; supersedes ADR-011 | Chosen |
| Memoise `renderMarkdown` per section, shared by both loaders | Keeps ADR-011; a module cache that grows in dev, and two copies of the HTML | Rejected |
| Do nothing | Two renders per section, Mermaid included | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- Each ADR section is rendered once per build.
- `RenderedAdr`'s `html` field goes.
- `adr-sections` is empty when the Decisions view is off, and
  `siteRefs()` already skips ADR keys then.
- Follows ADR-002 ADR sections export as Markdown text, ADR-006 Mermaid
  renders at build time with Pele, and ADR-012 The site reads image files
  beside an ADR.

adrs.title: Briefs and inbox files export ordered sections
adrs.context:
The docs site must show whole briefs and inbox files, and it reads
`planning.json` only. Today the export carries a brief's `problem`,
`doneWhen`, and `decision` first lines and an inbox file's `idea`. ADR-002
exports ADR sections as named Markdown fields.
adrs.decision:
Each brief and inbox entry in `planning.json` gains `sections`: an ordered
array of `{ heading, markdown }`, one per level-2 section after the header
block, in file order. The Markdown is verbatim, with HTML comments stripped
outside code and kept inside it. The existing summary fields stay. The
export moves to `schemaVersion` 6.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| An ordered `sections` list | Keeps every heading, including optional and consumer-added ones; the schema checks shape only | Chosen |
| One named field per heading, as ADRs have | 11 brief and 4 inbox fields; loses an unmodelled heading, as ADR-002 rejected structure | Rejected |
| Summary fields only (do nothing) | No export change, but a brief page adds little beyond Linked from | Rejected by the user (2026-11-26) |
adrs.consequences:
- The export grows by the text of every brief and inbox file.
- The schema, its example, the `pm-export` field map, and `planning.ts`
  change together.
- `@purview-dev/pm-docs-site` reads `schemaVersion` 6 from `0.1.0-pre.7`.
- Follows ADR-002 ADR sections export as Markdown text.

adrs.title: The site reads image files beside briefs and inbox files
adrs.context:
ADR-012 lets the site read the image files beside an ADR in
`<PM root>/decisions/`. Brief and inbox pages render their sections the
same way, and a section may reference a relative image.
adrs.decision:
`brief-sections` and `inbox-sections` content collections render each
section once with `renderMarkdown`, resolving relative images against
`briefs/<file>` or `inbox/<file>` beside the configured `planning.json`.
Linked from keys come from the same rendered HTML, as ADR-015 does for
ADRs. Every PM record is still read only from `planning.json`. A missing
image file fails the build.
adrs.alternatives:
| Approach | Trade-off | Outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Extend the ADR pipeline to briefs and inbox files | Same fidelity and link guarantees as ADR pages; two more collections | Chosen |
| Plain text through `LinkedText` | Cheaper; lists and tables flatten | Rejected |
| Read the brief and inbox Markdown files directly | Breaks the rule that the site reads the export only | Rejected |
adrs.consequences:
- Two more content collections, each empty when its view is off.
- Extends ADR-012 to two more folders without superseding it.
- Follows ADR-012 The site reads image files beside an ADR and ADR-015 ADR
  page references come from adr-sections.
